A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-function research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet, OpenWebText, and CIFAR-10 experiments, activation ablations, decision-boundary visualizations, and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical experiments with revised benchmark summaries and additionally reports CPU/GPU timing and MLP scaling results.

M1.justification: The activation definitions, practical implementations, interpolation procedures, and Algorithms 1–6 are retained. Making the Fourier sine-coefficient initialization explicit in the main text matches initialization already specified in v2 Appendix D; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1k, OpenWebText, noisy 2D classification, and ImageNet-to-CIFAR fine-tuning. The new timing sweeps vary computational settings without documenting new prediction tasks or datasets. Additional MNIST/SVHN discussion concerns other researchers' work.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets: GELU for ImageNet and fine-tuning, GELU/SiLU for GPT-2, and ConvNeXt-GELU plus ResNet50-ReLU for CIFAR-10. The timing study uses the existing GELU comparator and compares existing Hermite implementations. Newly cited activation methods are not added empirical baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix P introduces a substantial runtime evaluation design: forward-plus-backward timing across activation degrees on CPU/GPU, and per-epoch timing and relative slowdown across MLP widths 1024/2048/4096 and depths 8/16/32. Existing prediction-task configurations, including the CIFAR recipe and GPT-2 training budget, remain unchanged; replication changes are assessed under E5.

E4.justification: V3 adds systematic analyses of how runtime depends on activation degree, hardware, MLP width/depth, and explicit versus recursive Hermite implementation (Appendix P). These substantially extend the earlier complexity discussion. The four accuracy ablations in Tables 3–6 and the decision-boundary and fine-tuning experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Reported replication increases from three to five seeds for ImageNet and GPT-2, and from three to ten for CIFAR ConvNeXt; ResNet50 remains at three. Tables 1–2 replace standard-error captions with standard-deviation reporting, resolving their earlier disagreement with the prose. Tables 1, 2, and the CIFAR results table add two-tailed, equal-variance Student's t-tests against GELU. Plot shading remains min–max.

E6.justification: Benchmark summaries change with the larger seed sets. ImageNet Hermite/GELU Top-1 means change from 82.18/82.01 to 82.22/82.06. CIFAR's highest mean switches from Fourier (91.5 versus Hermite 91.4) to Hermite (91.35 versus Fourier 91.23). GPT-2 summaries also change. Appendix P adds substantial runtime and slowdown findings, while v2's separate seed-0 GPT-2 curve is removed.

T1.justification: Proposition D.7, Equation 67, gains the missing factor 1/2 in the Fourier forward/backward gain-equality condition, making it consistent with the preceding second-moment formulas. This is a limited mathematical correction; the broader theorem and proof framework, including Appendix F's polynomial-mapping argument, is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's main contribution claims remain unchanged. The conclusion adds a geometric characterization of hypothesis classes through algebraic varieties and tropical polyhedral complexes, and explicitly states its broad use of 'polynomial.' This modestly extends the contribution framing without introducing a new central method claim.

C2.justification: V3 replaces v2's general 30–90% training-overhead and inference-parity assertions with a depth-dependent runtime interpretation favoring shallow, wide MLPs. Appendix M adds critical-point and elliptic-curve-like interpretations of unchanged Hermite decision boundaries. These are targeted revisions to applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: The new timing material identifies an AMD EPYC 7402 CPU, an NVIDIA A100 with 40 GB memory, implementation variants, and per-epoch averaging. Existing training recipes and pseudocode are retained. The repository footnote now promises reproduction code but omits v2's explicit model-weight availability statement; the PDFs do not establish whether actual weight availability changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around neuroalgebraic geometry, identifiability, and loss landscapes, including Usevich et al. and Shahverdi et al. The extended related work adds earlier Hermite/Legendre activations, tropical activation research, and sinusoidal variance-preserving initialization, among other connections. These additions broaden attribution and scientific motivation beyond publication-year and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V3 applies targeted language polishing, softens passages criticizing KAN research, swaps the KAN and extended-related-work appendices, and revises Section 5 and the conclusion. The standalone Limitations and generic Impact Statement sections disappear, and an LLM-use disclosure is added. Most existing methodological and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds four timing figures and three timing tables, adds significance columns and metric-direction arrows to result tables, and redraws learning curves with revised legends and displayed ranges. Figure 3 changes from one row to a larger 2-by-2 arrangement. The single-seed GPT-2 plot is removed; the unchanged fine-tuning figure is renumbered. Conference formatting also substantially changes the document's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: More replication, consistent uncertainty reporting, and explicit tests strengthen confidence in the small benchmark differences. Correcting Equation 67 and adding measured runtime scaling improve mathematical consistency and practical guidance. These gains are limited by incomplete timing-workload details and overbroad CIFAR wording: v3 claims superiority across test metrics, although Table 7 reports Fourier Top-5 below GELU (99.60 versus 99.62).
